finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated into the query string. The attacker can inject SQL, e.g. subqueries or CASE expressions for boolean/blind extraction of data from any table readable via SQLite, or stacked/error-based tricks.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: concatenated directly into SQL passed to PDO::query()

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting or escaping in list_users_sorted. Prepared statements are not used for this query. The safe variant list_users_safe (line 9-13) uses an allowlist map, but this function does not. No authentication/authorization check exists in the file either.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 concatenates $_GET['sort'] into the ORDER BY with no allowlist, cast or parameterization (the allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe), but a grep finds no caller of list_users_sorted anywhere in the directory, so whether any entry point reaches it can't be determined from this code.
